centimeter: a unit of length measurement in the metric system (**100 centimeters** is equal to **1 meter**)
meter: a unit of length in the metric measurement system (**1 meter** is equal to **100 centimeters**)
acute angle: an angle with a measure of **less than 90 degrees**
angle: a geometric figure made up of **2 rays** that share the **same endpoint**
area: a measurement of the **space inside a two-dimensional shape**
attribute: a feature or trait of an object or set of objects
common denominator: when **2 or more fractions** have the **same denominator**
common multiple: a number that is a multiple of **2 or more given numbers**
common numerator: when **2 or more fractions** have the **same numerator**
composite number: a number that has **more than 1 factor pair**
decimal: a fractional value written using **single digits for each place value**
decimal point: a period placed to the **right of the ones place**
degree: a unit for measuring the size of an angle
denominator: the **bottom number** in a fraction that tells how many **equal parts** the whole was partitioned into
equivalent fractions: two fractions that represent the **same value**
expanded form: a representation of a number as an addition expression that shows **the value of each digit** (ex: 482 in expanded form is **400 + 80 + 2**)
factor pair: a set of **two numbers** that arrive at a specific number when multiplied (ex: 4 and 6 is a factor pair of 24)
horizontal: a straight line that goes from **left to right**
hundred thousands: the base-ten place value unit composed of **10 ten thousands** (one hundred thousand in standard form is **100,000**)
isosceles triangle: a triangle with exactly **2 equal-length sides**
kilometer: a unit of length in the metric measurement system (**1,000 meters** is equal to **1 kilometer**)
length: how long an object is from endpoint to endpoint (measured in same-length units with **no gaps or overlaps**)
line: a straight mark, sometimes connecting a set of points arranged side by side, that **extends infinitely in both directions**
line of symmetry: a line that splits a figure into **2 identical halves** that mirror each other
line segment or segment: a part of a line with **2 endpoints**
line symmetry: the quality of a shape that can be divided into **two identical or mirrored halves**
millileter: a unit of liquid volume in the metric measurement system (**1,000 millileters** is equal to **1 liter**)
million: the base-ten place value unit composed of **10 hundred thousands** (one million in standard form is **1,000,000**)
mixed number: a number expressed as a **whole number** and a **fraction less than 1**
multiple: a number you get by multiplying another number (ex: some multiples of 4 are **4, 8, 12, and 16**)
numerator: the **top number** in a fraction that tells how many of the **equal parts** are being described
obtuse angle: an angle with a measure **greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees**
ounce: a unit of weight in the U.S. customary measurement system (**16 ounces** is equal to **1 pound**)
parallelogram: a quadrilateral with **2 pairs of opposite sides** that are parallel
parentheses: **grouping symbols** that can be used in expressions or equations, ex: (3 x 5) + (2 x 10)
partial product: the value obtained when multiplying the parts of **2 numbers separately** (which is then added to other partial products to arrive at the total product)
partial quotient: the value obtained when multiplying the divisor in a division equation by another number, then subtracting that number from the dividend (which is then added to other partial quotients to arrive at the total quotient)
pattern: a specific, replicable sequence of shapes or numbers; some patterns **repeat** and some patterns **grow**
perimeter: the total length of the **boundary of a two-dimensional shape**
perpendicular line: a line that crosses another line at a **right angle**
pound: a unit of weight in the U.S. customary measurement system (**1 pound** is equal to **16 ounces**)
prime number: a number that has **only 1 factor pair**
protractor: a tool for measuring the size of an angle in degrees
quadrilateral: a shape with **4 sides** and **4 corners**
ray: a part of a line with **1 endpoint**
remainder: the amount leftover when another whole group of the divisor cannot be made when dividing
rounding: to estimate the value of a number by determining the nearest multiple of a specific place value
scalene triangle: a triangle with **no sides of equal length**
second: a unit of time (**60 seconds** is equal to **1 minute**)
standard form: a representation of a number using **only digits** to represent place values
ten thousand: the base-ten place value unit composed of **10 one thousands** (one ten thousand in standard form is **10,000**)
thousand: the base-ten place value unit composed of **10 hundreds** (one thousand in standard form is **1,000**)
unit fraction: a number that describes **exactly 1 part** of a whole that has been partitioned into **equal parts**
vertex: the point where **2 rays** of an angle meet (plural: vertices)
vertical: a straight line that goes from **up to down**
width: how wide an object is from side to side (measured in same-sized units with **no gaps or overlaps**)
yard: a unit of length in the U.S. customary measurement system (**1 yard** is equal to **three feet**)
